drivers.lead: Schneider took the outright record with his fourth in 2003 and stretched it to five in 2006
drivers.note: He is the only driver to have won the DTM in both of its lives: a first title in 1995, the last season before the original series collapsed into the ITC, then four more after it came back as the Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters in 2000. Eleven seasons separate his first from his last, and only 2000 and 2001 are back to back. The fifth, in 2006, came from two race wins. Before him the most anyone had managed was three, by Klaus Ludwig in 1988, 1992 and 1994, so Schneider equalled the record in 2001 and owned it alone from 2003. Nobody has come closer since. René Rast also has three, from 2017, 2019 and 2020, and went to the 2025 Hockenheim finale with a fourth still mathematically alive before a first-lap collision ended it; he left the series at the end of that season.

teams.lead: Mercedes-Benz has won the manufacturers' title in every era the DTM has had one, seventeen times in all, most recently in 2025
teams.note: The championship ran for seven seasons before it awarded a manufacturers' title at all, so the count starts in 1991 rather than 1984. Mercedes-Benz won four of the six given out in the original series — 1991, 1992, 1994 and 1995 — and thirteen of the twenty-six since the revival in 2000, including four straight from 2000 to 2003 and three straight from 2008 to 2010. Audi is closest on nine and won one as recently as 2022, so this is not a frozen record. The odd thing about the two most recent is that Mercedes-AMG took them without the drivers' title in either year: Mirko Bortolotti won the 2024 championship for Lamborghini and Ayhancan Güven the 2025 one for Porsche, while four Mercedes-AMG GT3s scored steadily enough across sixteen races to win the brands' count anyway.
